fit.gap_handling_summary: The CV makes a convincing, evidence-based case for AWS operations, Terraform, platform design, observability and technical leadership. It does not fabricate Terragrunt, mTLS, certificate management, JVM or fleet integration experience. However, neither document explicitly addresses the most important transfer gaps: secure remote-device connectivity and Terragrunt. Product leadership engagement is relevant transferable evidence, but is not equivalent to coordinating interfaces with train manufacturers.

artefacts: The extracted PDF contains joined words: “ReplacedanoisyNagiossetupwithPrometheus, Grafana, AlertmanagerandLokiformonitoringandalerting.”
issues: The certifications heading is stranded at the bottom of page one, with its entries on page two.
Page two is only 14.6% filled; the nominally acceptable two-page length is poorly balanced.
The internal developer platform project repeats substantial detail already given under Tallybrook.
The two-sentence summary meets the request, but its second sentence remains long and densely packed.

keywords_missing_but_candidate_has: networking — relevant AWS VPC and Route 53 skills are listed, but the broader keyword is not explicit
reasons: Coverage counts clear semantic equivalents: platform design for system design, technical lead for technical leadership, product-leadership agreement for stakeholder engagement, EC2 for virtual machines, and Terraform modules for infrastructure as code.
AWS and substantial Terraform experience are prominent and quantified.
Terragrunt and secure-connectivity terms are absent; a strict must-have filter could reject the application.
The PDF has a sensible overall reading order, but one monitoring bullet fails the words-intact criterion because several words are concatenated.
Single-column structure, standard headings and explicit employment dates otherwise support extraction.

issues: Beyond the company name and exact role title, the letter does not use distinctive company facts or explain interest in Corvale's new train fleet.
It concentrates on internal developer platforms without making a sufficiently concrete bridge to train-to-cloud connectivity.
Terragrunt, mTLS and certificate-management gaps are left unaddressed.
The long Tallybrook paragraph and conclusion repeat platform design, production readiness and product-team support.
strengths: Uses the correct company and contractor role.
Presents strong, supported AWS, Terraform, scale and reliability evidence.
Explains stakeholder engagement through the real error-budget policy example.
Correctly treats Brightwater as previous employment rather than reusing the earlier letter's outdated present-tense framing.
Maintains a professional tone and fits on one page.

overflow_or_cutoff: Several CV section rules visibly cross the lower portions of heading lettering, including PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY, TECHNICAL SKILLS and PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE.
spacing_issues: CV page one is densely packed while page two is only 14.6% filled.
CERTIFICATIONS is orphaned at the bottom of page one; its rule and entries continue on page two.
The repeated internal developer platform project consumes space that could help avoid the sparse second page.
consistency_issues: The cleanup-operator and speaking entries use a colon after the date, whereas the internal developer platform entry uses an em dash.
issues: The CV's 10-point body and dense first page are readable but provide limited scanning space.
The cover letter is clean, consistently set in 11-point text, and has no visible cutoff or overlap.
Both documents use compatible serif typography, but the CV's heading-rule placement needs correction.

fluency_and_tone_issues: “Technical lead for a five-person platform team, experienced in cloud infrastructure and platform design and operation...” is a heavily packed summary sentence.

“This work involved designing platform interfaces, self-service infrastructure, and an operating model ... giving me practical experience translating platform design decisions into an operable system” is abstract and repetitive.
“from system design through production” and “from design through production” recur in the final paragraph without adding evidence.

notes_facts_used: Mentored three engineers from backend into SRE.
Spoke at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024 on “SLOs that product managers care about.”
Preserved Senior Platform Engineer as the formal title while describing technical leadership, without claiming line management.
Kept Backstage limited to catalog use.
Did not list the expired CKAD or claim production Istio, Linkerd, Azure or GCP experience.

The tool replied, “Your updated CV and cover letter are ready.”
requests.note: The final summary contains exactly two sentences. Its second sentence is long, but the requested sentence limit is met.

requests.request: Thanks. Now please move the skills section above the work experience.

requests.note: The earlier two-sentence summary change is preserved. Only the final versions are available, so unrelated changes between intermediate versions cannot be independently checked.

evaluation.summary: Both documents faithfully present the candidate's strong AWS, Terraform, platform engineering and reliability experience, and both requested CV changes are preserved. The application is less convincing on the role's distinctive requirements: Terragrunt, secure train-to-cloud communication, certificate management and remote-device integration are not addressed. The cover letter is accurate but largely generic beyond the role title and company name. The main presentation defects are the CV's nearly empty second page, orphaned certifications heading, heading-rule collisions and one PDF extraction error.
